title: Matched Allen cortical recordings do not resolve a source-versus-target difference in synaptic delay similarity
abstract: We tested whether connections with one source cell have more similar delays than connections with one target cell. We used the Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 database and compared both structures within each recording, synapse sign, and ordered cell-class group. Mouse visual cortex supplied 82 matched groups from 74 inferred animals. The target-minus-source contrast in mean squared log delay was 0.00455, with a 95% cluster bootstrap interval of -0.06872 to 0.07775. After donor-held-out adjustment for distance and cell features, the contrast was -0.01430, with an interval of -0.07297 to 0.04426. Fifteen human groups from ten inferred donors also gave intervals that include zero. A delay-range check did not change the conclusion. This test does not resolve which shared cell end gives more similar delays. It does not show equal variation. Sparse matched graphs, uncertain donor labels, response fit error, and slice conditions limit the result. We provide a reproducible graph comparison, cohort identifiers, group results, uncertainty draws, and source provenance.

display.caption: The target-sharing minus source-sharing contrast in squared log delay. Bars show 95% inferred-donor bootstrap intervals. Positive values favor more similar delays from one source. All intervals include zero.
